newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Radiomobil to launch mobile service Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: Czech Radiomobil to launch mobile service Sept 27.

text.p: The operator of the second Czech digital GSM mobile phone network, RadioMobil a.s., said on Monday it will launch its service "Paegas" on September 27.
"We are planning to start the service on Friday, the 27th," RadioMobil's spokeswoman, Tereza Kakosova said. She declined to detail the company's final price for the service.
RadioMobil, which won a government tender for its licence earlier this year, has promised to be competitive with EuroTel which started its GSM service in July.
Eurotel is a joint venture between Czech SPT Telecom a.s., U.S. Bell Atlantic Corp and U.S. West Media Group.
EuroTel has already been cutting its rates in anticipation of a price war with Paegas.

In its initial stages of operation, Paegas plans to cover major Czech cities with its signal. The company expects it signal will cover 80 percent of Czech territory by mid-year next year, and then cover more remote areas, raising penetration to 90 percent of the territory by first quarter 1999.

RadioMobil includes the Czech transmission firm Ceske Radiokomunikace a.s. which holds 51 percent, and the international consortium TMobil led by Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG along with Italy's Stet SpA.

TMobil won a government tender for the second GSM network licence last spring, promising to invest 5.5 billion Czech crowns in the European standard digital network, and laying out a strict tariff structure.
